scores.rationale: Technically sound on what the design depends on (pgvector, hybrid search, alias rollback, output filter against exfil links/images); minor imprecision such as 'zero PII in sampled logs' and no treatment of embedding-vendor data flows.

scores.evidence: Does the bot act on accounts (order status, refunds)? I assume no: read-only Q&A plus handoff.
scores.rationale: Covers core RAG, citations, handoff, deletion, with explicit deferrals and reasons; minor gaps are no explicit escalation triggers beyond confirm/unsure and no stated deletion time window.
Consistent design with clear phases and ownership; small loose ends such as Phase 0 'employees' versus Phase 4 'logged-in visitors' and 24h session memory versus 30-day transcripts.

scores.evidence: SMEs grade the 200 queries plus 50 "policy-bait" prompts
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks (worst failure, injection, PII, cost), with measurable thresholds labeled ASSUMPTION, early deploy/rollback check, vendor trial, canary and post-launch reviews; only a weak point is that regression re-run on every change is implied rather than explicit.

scores.evidence: Peak concurrent chats: comes from Support analytics, needed by Phase 4 | UNKNOWN
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are explicitly labeled with their consequences (e.g., account actions add an auth phase) and revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Injection suite in CI, covering both user text and instructions planted in docs.
scores.rationale: Covers hallucinated policy, injection, exfil links, PII, LLM outage, feedback poisoning, with detection and rollback; thin on stale-content detection, index partial-sync failure, and sync failure alerts.

scores.evidence: blue/green deploy through CI/CD. Each request gets an OpenTelemetry trace with retrieved chunk IDs, tokens, cost and latency.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, alerts, flag kill switch, review queue are concrete; incident ownership/on-call and alerting on quality signals are not explicit.

scores.evidence: Cost per resolved conversation | Must beat the cost of a human-handled ticket
scores.rationale: Drivers and controls (token caps, session cap, routing, build-vs-buy) are identified, but there is no per-conversation cost estimate or range on a stated basis; it is left UNKNOWN.

scores.evidence: Hosted API behind a provider-agnostic interface
scores.rationale: Decisions are explicitly tagged by reversibility, with pinned embeddings, versioned indexes, exit paths to self-host or buy, and deferrals; effort is concentrated on the one-way decisions.
Starts from the simplest design (single service, pgvector, no fine-tuning, no routing), with growth triggers; phase-level ceremony is moderate but justified.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 ... about 20 ingested public articles in pgvector ... Exit check: V0.
scores.rationale: Thin first slice, phases ordered by dependency with exit checks, rollback per phase, and explicit adaptation paths if checks fail.
